page: Amazon Web Services i3en.12xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is substantial at 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. A key architectural characteristic is the inclusion of 30,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage paired with a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system does not feature dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results show balanced aggregate multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread metrics. Stress-ng single-core performance scores 1379.2, placing it in the lower 25% bracket, while multi-core stress testing reaches 40663.15 in the middle 50% percentile. Memory bandwidth reflects 110.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 49.34 GB/sec for writes. Database operations in PassMark register at 15612.36, and the instance achieves 38.4 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, bolstered by the high memory and fast bus speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i3en.12xlarge delivers dense local NVMe storage combined with a balanced compute and memory allocation, eliminating the need to provision expensive external block storage arrays for high-throughput applications. A tradeoff exists in per-core compute performance, as older architecture yields weaker single-thread execution and slower compression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip at 23.58 GB/sec.

This server profile is structured for high-capacity, I/O-intensive workloads requiring rapid access to massive local storage. It serves distributed file systems, data warehousing, large relational or NoSQL databases, search indexing clusters, and high-throughput data processing applications.
